name: Chandīgarh
summary_text: This union territory was covered by the dedicated country dossier, which identified no deviation from the national position material enough to score separately (±0.02); it is therefore assessed at the national score. Its one unit-level signal is official-will positive: Chandīgarh is among only 12 of India's 36 states/UTs that have constituted the transgender welfare board required by the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Rules, 2020 — though an RTI investigation found most such boards rudderless, without a policy framework, compliance mechanism or real power.

sources.title: Transgender Bill: India parliament passes amendment to redefine transgender identity amid protests
sources.claim_summary: BBC report (26 March 2026): India's parliament passed a bill amending the 2019 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act that removes the right to self-identify, limits recognition to biological/physical traits (including intersex variations and traditional community identities) certified by medical boards and district authorities, and mandates certification for gender-affirming surgery; protests followed, the estimated ~2 million transgender population faces uneven recognition, and a Supreme Court-appointed panel asked the government to withdraw the bill as contrary to the 2014 self-identification ruling.

Times of India city report (18 August 2024): a transwoman alleged a railway-police constable groped her as a 'gender check' at a Kolkata metro station and made a lewd remark; the railway police denied it and filed a counter-FIR — recorded as an instance of security-force practice treating trans presentation as itself grounds for invasive 'gender verification' at transport checkpoints, in a case that reached the courts on the complainants' side.
